title: Was Malthus right about carrying capacity?
summary: Josh and Chuck examine whether Thomas Malthus was right about carrying capacity and population growth. They cover Malthus's exponential-vs-linear argument and his 18th-century debate with William Godwin, the demographic transition and replacement fertility rate, Norman Borlaug and the Green Revolution as technological escapes from the Malthusian trap, estimates of Earth's carrying capacity (roughly two to forty billion depending on lifestyle), resource inequality, and whether greed or human ingenuity will decide the outcome. The episode closes with a listener mail about a Portland mother who sneakily got her teenage son to listen to the show.

entities.name: An Essay on the Principle of Population
The Worst Mistake in the History of the Human Race

segments.title: Opening banter and introduction to carrying capacity
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open with banter about Josh's verbal habits, then Josh describes learning about carrying capacity in an anthropology class, Jared Diamond's essay, and a map video of population spreading across the globe.

segments.title: Population statistics and exponential growth
segments.summary: The hosts cite UN population figures, the approach to seven billion people, and population growth from under a billion in 1800 to billions by 1960. They explain exponential growth versus linear growth.

segments.title: Thomas Malthus and his critics
segments.summary: They introduce Thomas Malthus, his 18th-century essay on population, his debate with William Godwin and the perfectibility of society, and the links to eugenics, anarchism, and rent theory.

segments.title: Demographic transition and replacement rate
segments.summary: They discuss how falling mortality and fertility rates, birth control, and education have changed population trends, including the replacement rate of 2.1 children and current fertility rates in Europe, Asia, and sub-Saharan Africa.

segments.title: Agriculture, Green Revolution and Norman Borlaug
segments.summary: They describe how the carrying capacity of hunter-gatherers was about 100 million people, how agriculture and the Green Revolution, led by Norman Borlaug, raised food yields and averted predicted famine.

segments.title: Estimated carrying capacity and lifestyle
segments.summary: They present estimates of Earth's carrying capacity ranging from two to forty billion, explaining that the spread depends on lifestyle, resource consumption by middle-class Americans, and the minimum food and water requirements, including the meat and grain issue.

segments.title: Technology, greed and debate on responsibility
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck discuss using technology to get more from less versus more from more, mountaintop removal, renewable energy, the EV1 electric car, and whether responsibility for conservation lies with individuals or policy makers.
